name: Flat-price outbound webhooks with DPA included for small API vendors
buyer: Seed-stage SaaS or API company with 1-2 engineers that must send signed, retried webhooks to its own customers, with a customer portal and GDPR paperwork
pain: Cost steps up sharply after the free tier, and the DPA (GDPR processor paperwork) sits behind Svix's $490/mo Professional plan.
wedge: Flat ~$29/mo plan that includes a signed DPA and 100k messages, aimed at EU-leaning small API vendors who only need outbound webhooks.

scan1Edge.entrant_basis: Sell a flat $29/mo plan with a templated DPA bundled, using cheap managed hosting and a queue. No sales or enterprise tier is needed.
scan1Edge.falsifier: Hook0, Hook Mesh and EventDock already sell near-identical flat plans at $29-59. If a buyer can get a DPA from them at similar prices, or Svix adds DPA to Basic, the edge disappears.
scan1Edge.unit: USD per month for a plan that includes a DPA (~100k messages)

unitEconomicsNoted.notes: ESTIMATE from research notes: margin ~75-85% at low volume. Price is the proposed wedge price, not validated.

majorUncertainty: Whether anonymous solo-run delivery infrastructure can earn trust (SLA, SOC 2) when at least four cheaper entrants already exist.
unknowns: Whether Svix, Hookdeck and the cheaper entrants verified prices on vendor pages match the third-party comparison pages
Real willingness to pay for DPA-included small plans
Whether a solo founder can credibly promise an uptime SLA
Actual SOC 2 requirement among target buyers
Svix free-tier limits are disputed (50 vs 200 msg/s)
regulatoryOrPlatformDependency: Depends on cloud hosting. GDPR/DPA expectations apply. Buyers may ask for SOC 2 and an uptime SLA. Delivery to customer-supplied endpoints carries abuse and SSRF risk.
